# Forms and fields

> Settled 2026-09-09. Answers `analysis/ui/FORMS_AND_FIELDS.md` §§ 3, 6 and 7.

## 1. Required is an asterisk, and nothing else

Every required field carries a `*` after its label. The asterisk is **grey and unobtrusive** — it is
a marker, not a warning, and it appears on most fields on most forms, so drawing it in red shouts at
somebody who has done nothing wrong.

```tsx
<Label htmlFor={id}>
  Name <span className="text-muted-foreground">*</span>
</Label>
```

The wrapper is `RequiredLabel` — `Label` plus the grey `*`. Use it; `Label` was imported in 47 files
with nothing wrapping it, which is why four conventions grew instead of one.

**Optional fields are marked by the absence of the asterisk.** Nothing else.

**The one exception: the sign-in screens** — a company's login, "sign in to your company", "find your
company" (owner, 2026-09-22). One or two fields, every one of them required and obviously so; the
asterisk there is noise on the one screen everybody sees first. They use plain `Label`. A screen that
asks for more than that — registration, the setup wizard — is a form, and the rule applies.

**Required means *you must supply this*, not *this ends up non-null*.** A field that is pre-filled and
cannot be emptied — the termination `Reason`, a policy's `Effective From` — carries no asterisk: the
mark would promise a demand the form never makes. Which field is required is read from the form's own
validation — its Yup schema, or its hand-written checks.

### What this replaces

Four conventions, none dominant: an asterisk in the label; HTML `required` with **no visual marker at
all** (16 fields on the legal-entity form alone — ten of them required, and nothing on screen said so
until submit); `placeholder="Optional"` marking the *optional* ones instead; and `Password*` written
inside the placeholder.

## 2. No placeholders

**Fields have no placeholder text.** Not an example value, not `e.g. Engineering`, not `Optional`.

Three reasons, in order of weight:

1. **A placeholder disappears when you type**, so any information in it is gone exactly when it might
   be checked. A hint that vanishes on first keystroke is not a hint.
2. **The product used placeholders for three different jobs at once** — an example value, a
   requiredness marker, and a label substitute — so the same grey text meant three things. It even
   split by module: offices and legal entities wrote `e.g., London HQ`, departments and the job
   catalog wrote `e.g. Engineering`, one comma apart.
3. Grey text inside a field reads as a filled value to enough people that it costs support time.

Where a field genuinely needs explaining, use **helper text under the field** — visible, persistent,
and announced.

**The two exceptions**, and they are exceptions because they are not fields in a form:

- **Search boxes**, whose placeholder is the word `Search` ([`ACTIONS_AND_MENUS.md`](ACTIONS_AND_MENUS.md) § 4).
- **Selects**, which need a "nothing chosen yet" state the control cannot otherwise express.

**And one owner-asked exception inside a form** (2026-09-26, kept 2026-09-28): the Attendance tab's
**Quick Fill** shows the last span logged as the empty form's placeholders, with a Quick Fill button that
confirms them. It is not an example value — it is an offer of the person's own last entry, and the button
beside it says so. Nothing else in the product does this; it is not a pattern to copy.

## 3. No "Optional" anywhere

Remove `Optional` and `(optional)` from every label, hint and placeholder. § 1 says optional is the
absence of the asterisk; saying it twice, in a different vocabulary, in a different place, is how the
seven `placeholder="Optional"` sites and the seven `(optional)` labels came to disagree.

## 4. Empty values are empty

**A missing value renders as an empty cell.** No em dash, no `No manager`, no `Not set`.

The product had `—` in tables and sentence-form absence on the profile (`No manager`, `No job`,
`No office`, `No legal entity`, `No department`) — so the same missing fact looked like two different
kinds of fact one click apart.

An empty cell is unambiguous: there is nothing there. A dash is a character somebody has to learn
means nothing, and it is indistinguishable from a value that genuinely is a dash. This applies to
**both** tables and the person profile.

**Not every dash is an empty value.** An avatar that shows a dash in place of a missing initial is
drawing a letter, not an empty cell, and keeps it.

## 5. The None option is `None`

A select that allows "no value" offers one option labelled exactly **`None`**.

Radix `Select` cannot hold an empty string, so every module invented its own sentinel *and* its own
label: `ROOT_VALUE = "none"` on departments and teams, `"No category"` on leave types and documents,
`"No folder"` on the document move and upload dialogs, `"No level"` on jobs. Four labels for one
idea.

The sentinel value stays an implementation detail — `NONE_VALUE`, shared from `models/select` — but
**what the reader sees is the word `None`**.

## 6. A duration is `H:MM`

A length of time — logged, expected, a norm, overtime — is written **hours, a colon, two-digit minutes**:
`7:30`, `0:05`, `160:00`. Not `7.5`, not `7.50`, not `7h 30m`. Decided for Attendance on 2026-09-28;
the helper is `formatMinutes` in `models/attendance`, and durations travel as minutes so nothing has to
round. A field that takes a duration accepts `7:30` and `7.5` alike (`parseDuration`).

Two spellings of one quantity one click apart was the reason: the old timesheet said `8`, the profile tab
`8.00`. Leave is counted in **days**, not durations, and keeps its own format (`formatDayAmount`).

## 7. A vocabulary is a plain select, data is a searchable one (decided 2026-10-27)

**The product's own short list is a plain `Select`; a list that is data is the searchable select**
(`components/ui/SearchableSelect` — a `Popover` + `Command` with a search field).

- **Plain** — the product's vocabulary, two to eight options that never grow: date format, first day of
  the week, approval mode, who sees a document, when a lifecycle task is due, an attribute's type, how a
  balance accrues, a status in a filter.
- **Searchable** — the world's lists (countries, time zones, languages, currencies) and the company's
  (people, jobs, departments, teams, offices, leave types), **however short they are today**: a company
  with five departments gets a search box over five items, which costs nothing, and the field does not
  change its look when the sixteenth office is added.

The line is drawn by meaning, not by a count, so it is known when the field is written. The owner looked
at the control on 2026-11-01, and every data select moved onto it the same day. Two lists that come from
the server stay plain on purpose, because they are the product's vocabulary served as data: the Logs
page's modules, actions and verbs, and the role templates on *Add role*.

What the control carries for the lists it took over: an option `group` (job levels under their level
group), a `depth` (a department under its parent), `disabled` items, and `aria-label` / `aria-invalid`.
A "None" choice is an option like any other, with `clearable={false}`, so a field that offered "None"
still does. Tests swap it for a native `<select>` with `@/test/searchableSelectMock`. The list's scrollbar
is a thumb only, shown while the list moves (`DECISIONS.md` § "Owner decisions of 2026-11-01").

## What this does not settle

- ~~Helper text size~~ — settled by the design system (2026-11-04): a field's hint is `text-hint
  text-tertiary`, and its error replaces the hint (`FieldError`, SPEC § 12).
- Which conceptual fields are an `Input` and which a `Textarea` — Description is both, by module.
- The select placeholder wording (`Select…`, `Select field`, `Select a field`, `Pick a family` — four
  verbs for one action).
- The hand-rolled `StrategyOption` "radio that is not a radio" on offices and legal entities.
- `OptionsEditor`, whose rows are numbered through the placeholder (`Option 1`, `Option 2`) — the only
  label those inputs have, so § 2 cannot simply strip it. Real labels there are a design change.

## Something people must do is a choice per item

From the designers' company hub round (`hris/design/handoffs/2026-11-12-company-hub/PRODUCT-RULES.md`), taken by the owner on 2026-11-12 (CH7).

- **An obligation is optional per item**, switched on where it is needed, with a hint about when to leave it off —
  "Must read" on a page: "Turn it off for pages that are only for reference, like guides or office info."
